confidence_basis: Main PDF, OpenDataLoader markdown, pypdf fallback text, rendered methods/design pages, extracted Figure 1 image, supplement DOCX/text extraction, and the Canzoneri 2012 lineage review were checked. The paper reports enough Segment 1-4 information to recreate Exp. 1 and Exp. 2 as separate two-speaker looming/receding arm-movement profiles. Remaining uncertainty concerns exact original WAV/noise seeds, speaker model, full acoustic transfer, exact gain-curve files, and numeric ITI/jitter beyond participant-triggered trial starts.

profile_recreation_assessment.reason: Exp. 1 and Exp. 2 can be recreated as sagittal two-speaker pink-noise looming/receding profiles with separate durations, tactile-delay schedules, unisensory baselines, block structures, and trial counts. The profile should preserve the motor/static and hand/trunk block factors while treating original audio files, exact speaker acoustics, gain-curve files, and numeric ITI/jitter as approximations.

orientation_ledger.participant_frame: Blindfolded participant seated at a table, facing the two-speaker line in front of the body; right hand rests on/holds the mouse on the sagittal movement path, left hand responds on the keyboard.
orientation_ledger.room_apparatus_frame: Two physical speakers are positioned along the sagittal plane in front of the participant, 100 cm apart. The near speaker is 10 cm from the right hand; the motor barrier is 30 cm away on the table.
orientation_ledger.body_relative_mapping: Looming is far-to-near/towards the participant's body; receding is near-to-far/away from the participant. For receding T1-T5 map to D1-D5; for looming the mapping is flipped from D5 to D1.
orientation_ledger.tactile_anchor: Electrical tactile targets are delivered either to the radial aspect of the right index finger or to the center of the chest/trunk, in separate body-part blocks.
orientation_ledger.movement_implementation: Apparent auditory motion is implemented by reciprocal near/far speaker gain envelopes. Right-hand movement is a separate motor manipulation, tracked with E-Prime at 20 Hz.
orientation_ledger.evidence_class: Main-text methods, Figure 1 caption/image, rendered PDF pages 3-5, supplement distance-localization pilot text, and Canzoneri 2012 protocol lineage review.

Used as the primary extracted-text map for five semantic searches over stimulus reconstruction, spatial geometry, timing/SOA, sequence/intermixing, baseline/catch/counts, and tactile apparatus.
Visual inspection of Figure 1 to confirm participant-facing direction, sagittal speaker line, 100 cm speaker separation, timing panels, and motor/static hand/trunk conditions.
Checked local supplement for sound-distance pilot, expectancy analyses, outlier checks, and movement-variability analyses; no original stimulus scripts or WAV files were present.
Searched T1-T5, looming, receding, trial, baseline, catch, motor variability, and sound-distance localization terms.
Printed targeted snippets from PDF pages 3-6 to verify acoustic setup, tactile calibration, procedure, block formulas, Table 1, response/scoring window, and missing ITI/jitter.
Temporary rendered pages were visually checked for Figure 1 geometry, methods text, Table 1, and design/count paragraphs; page images were not committed.
Checked the cited Canzoneri 2012 procedure lineage for two-speaker pink-noise/gain conventions and unresolved original stimulus-file caveats.

review_attempts.result: Mapped 17/25 auto-mined candidate fields and identified the need to separate auditory apparent-motion speed from participant arm-movement speed.
Confirmed MATLAB/Audacity 44.1 kHz pink noise, two sagittal speakers, 55-70 dB reciprocal gain envelopes, 3000 ms Exp. 1 sounds, and 4000 ms Exp. 2 sounds.
Inspected Figure 1 and rendered methods pages; recorded participant facing, speaker/source room layout, body-relative looming/receding mapping, tactile anchors, and motor manipulation.
Separated Exp. 1 T1-T5 audio-tactile timing plus T1/T5 tactile-only baseline from Exp. 2's five matched audio-tactile and unisensory timings.

review_attempts.strategy: Trial sequence, intermixing, and count pass
review_attempts.result: Confirmed separated body-part/hand-status blocks, looming/receding and distance rows within audio-tactile blocks, catch trials, randomized/counterbalanced block presentation, and Exp. 1/2 totals.
Supplement confirmed the T1-T5 perceived-distance pilot and movement analyses but did not provide original stimulus files, scripts, speaker model, or ITI/jitter values.
pypdf snippets and rendered PDF pages 3-5 verified methods/table text and supported marking numeric ITI/jitter as not reported after review.
Canzoneri 2012 lineage supports the two-speaker gain-envelope convention, but exact author audio files and gain-curve files remain unavailable.

stimulus_type.evidence_note: The paper reports pink-noise samples generated for both experiments.

source_provenance.value: Pink-noise samples generated using MATLAB 2022b and Audacity 2.4.1; exact WAV files or random seeds are not supplied.
source_provenance.page_or_section: PDF p.3, Acoustic stimuli; supplement searched
source_provenance.evidence_note: Software provenance is reported; supplement does not add original stimulus files.

trajectory_count.value: Two auditory directions on the same two-speaker path: looming and receding. Exp. 1 and Exp. 2 use the same path but different sound durations/timing schedules.
trajectory_count.page_or_section: PDF p.3 Acoustic stimuli; PDF p.4 Design
trajectory_count.evidence_note: Motor/static and hand/trunk are block factors, not additional auditory trajectories.

trajectory_path.value: Two speakers along the sagittal plane in front of the participant, 100 cm apart; near speaker 10 cm from the right hand. Looming is far-to-near/towards body; receding is near-to-far/away.
trajectory_path.page_or_section: PDF p.3 Acoustic stimuli and Figure 1; Figure 1a
trajectory_path.evidence_note: Figure 1 confirms blindfolded participant facing the sagittal speaker line.

stimulus_duration.value: Exp. 1 auditory stimulus duration was 3000 ms; Exp. 2 auditory stimulus duration was 4000 ms.
stimulus_duration.evidence_note: Exp. 2 was lengthened to avoid too-early T1 during movement.

stimulus_speed.value: No explicit auditory-source speed is reported; nominal apparent path is 100 cm over 3 s in Exp. 1 (33.3 cm/s) and 100 cm over 4 s in Exp. 2 (25 cm/s).
stimulus_speed.page_or_section: PDF p.3 Acoustic stimuli; PDF p.4 General procedure
stimulus_speed.evidence_note: The reported 10 and 7.5 cm/s values are hand-movement speeds, not sound speeds.

auditory_conditions.value: Looming and receding sounds are included in audio-tactile blocks; sounds are task-irrelevant and crossed with hand/trunk tactile site and motor/static block factors.
auditory_conditions.page_or_section: PDF p.3 Acoustic stimuli; PDF p.4 Design
auditory_conditions.evidence_note: Within audio-tactile blocks, both sound directions and five sound distances are included.

gain_envelope.value: One stream exponentially increases 55 to 70 dB SPL and the other decreases 70 to 55 dB. Looming fades far speaker down and near speaker up; receding reverses it.
gain_envelope.evidence_note: SPL was measured at subjects' ears; exact envelope files are not provided.

renderer_or_apparatus.value: Two physical speakers on a sagittal/front path, MATLAB/Audacity stimulus generation, SPL audiometer calibration, E-Prime movement tracking, Logitech K120 response keyboard.
renderer_or_apparatus.evidence_note: Speaker model and room transfer are not reported.

trial_rows_families.value: Audio-tactile target trials, auditory-only catch trials inside audio-tactile blocks, and tactile-only unisensory baseline blocks.
trial_rows_families.evidence_note: Audio-tactile and unisensory trials were not intermixed.

condition_intermixing.value: Within each audio-tactile block, looming/receding and five distance rows were included. Body part and hand status were separated into trunk motor, trunk static, hand motor, and hand static blocks.
condition_intermixing.evidence_note: Unisensory tactile blocks were separated from audio-tactile blocks.

blocked_or_random_order.value: Exp. 1 used 4 audio-tactile blocks and 8 unisensory blocks; Exp. 2 used 4 audio-tactile blocks and 4 unisensory blocks. Block presentation was randomized/counterbalanced.
blocked_or_random_order.evidence_note: Exp. 1 also reports unisensory blocks before and after audio-tactile blocks.

iti_jitter_policy.evidence_note: No numeric ITI/jitter found; only participant-triggered trial start is reported.

response_window.value: Responses were left-key keyboard presses; analysis excluded RTs shorter than 100 ms or longer than 1000 ms. No separate online timeout is reported.
response_window.page_or_section: PDF p.4 General procedure; PDF p.5 Statistical analyses
response_window.evidence_note: The 100-1000 ms interval is a scoring/exclusion window.

task_sequence_rules.value: Participants responded only to tactile stimuli, ignored sounds, withheld responses on auditory-only catches, and started each trial by mouse key in Exp. 1 or pedal release in Exp. 2.
task_sequence_rules.evidence_note: Motor trials required 30 cm sagittal hand movement over the sound duration.

tactile_stimulus.value: Electrocutaneous pulses from Digitimer DS7A/D188; electrodes on right index finger radial aspect or center chest; 100 us trunk pulse, 200 us finger pulse, individually calibrated.
tactile_stimulus.evidence_note: Calibration used ascending limits and 10/10 detection before blocks.

soa_table.value: Exp. 1 audio-tactile delays: 300, 800, 1500, 2200, 2700 ms. Exp. 2 delays: 800, 1300, 2000, 2700, 3200 ms from sound onset.
soa_table.evidence_note: T1-T5 map to D1-D5 for receding and D5-D1 for looming.

baseline_strategy.value: Separate tactile-only unisensory baseline blocks. Exp. 1 baselines only at endpoint timings; Exp. 2 baselines matched all five audio-tactile delays.
baseline_strategy.evidence_note: Exp. 2 used matched unisensory RT subtraction for expectancy correction.

baseline_timing.value: Exp. 1 tactile-only baseline used T1 300 ms and T5 2700 ms from trial initiation. Exp. 2 baseline used 800, 1300, 2000, 2700, and 3200 ms from trial initiation.
baseline_timing.page_or_section: PDF p.4, Tactile timing; PDF pp.4-5 Design
baseline_timing.evidence_note: No-sound baselines are timed from trial initiation rather than sound onset.

catch_trial_type.value: Auditory-only catch trials in audio-tactile blocks, with no tactile stimulation and no response required.
catch_trial_type.page_or_section: PDF p.4 General procedure; PDF pp.4-5 Design
catch_trial_type.evidence_note: Catch trials are excluded from unisensory tactile blocks.

repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.value: Exp. 1: 15 trials for each audio-tactile direction x distance row; unisensory blocks have 6 trials at T1 and 6 at T5. Exp. 2: 10 trials per audio-tactile row and 10 per unisensory delay.
repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.evidence_note: Counts are reported per condition and block family.

baseline_count.value: Exp. 1 has 8 unisensory blocks x 12 trials = 96 baseline trials. Exp. 2 has 4 unisensory blocks x 50 trials = 200 baseline trials.
baseline_count.evidence_note: Baseline blocks are tactile-only and separated from audio-tactile blocks.

catch_count.value: Exp. 1 has 16 catches per audio-tactile block x 4 blocks = 64 catches. Exp. 2 has 10 catches per audio-tactile block x 4 blocks = 40 catches.
catch_count.evidence_note: Per-block catch counts are reported; totals are simple multiplication.

block_count.value: Exp. 1: 4 audio-tactile blocks plus 8 unisensory blocks. Exp. 2: 4 audio-tactile blocks plus 4 unisensory blocks.
block_count.evidence_note: Audio-tactile blocks correspond to trunk/hand x motor/static.

total_trial_count.value: Exp. 1 grand total is 760 trials: 664 audio-tactile/catch trials plus 96 unisensory trials. Exp. 2 grand total is 640 trials: 440 plus 200.

critical_caveats: The exact original pink-noise WAV files, random/noise seeds, and gain-envelope files are not provided.
The speaker model, room acoustics, and full acoustic transfer function are not reported.
The auditory apparent-motion speed is derived from speaker separation and duration; the reported 10/7.5 cm/s values are arm-movement speeds.
No numeric ITI, jitter range, or inter-trial distribution was found; trials are participant-triggered by mouse press or pedal release.
Exp. 1 and Exp. 2 should be implemented as separate profiles because duration, tactile timings, baseline strategy, and trial counts differ.
Exp. 1 reports unisensory blocks before and after audio-tactile blocks while also stating randomized/counterbalanced block presentation; exact run-order constraints should be approximated.
The supplement verifies subjective distance and movement analyses but does not contain scripts or original stimuli.
